And if God—praise be to His Name!—had not cast a pestilence into it,
after years they would not have been able to conquer it.
And when, as by a divine sign, the majority of the people within it perished,
and the Sultan himself also died,
Malik Muzaffar, his son, came down,
and surrendered the fortress.
And the King of Kings magnified him and honored him very greatly,
and loved him,
and set him in authority.
Kitbuqa, however, searched and found the place where Malik Nasir was hiding in the desert.
And he sent an army against him and captured him,
and seized him and brought him to himself,
and with care sent him to the King of Kings.
And when he came to him,
he received him joyfully and honored him,
and promised him that he would restore his kingdom to him once again.
And in those days, Rabban Simeon, the priest and physician, son of Rabban Yeshu the priest of blessed memory, from Qal'ah Rumayta, was brought to the service of the King of Kings Hulagu.
And he grew great and achieved high renown,
and was beloved by all the princes and queens.
And there belonged to him royal courtyards, gardens, orchards, and villas in Maraghah,
and pensions,
five thousand dinars each year,
from Babel, Assyria, Cappadocia, and from Maraghah itself; and through him there came great help, lifting up of the head, and honor to the remnant of our people,
and stability and protection for our Church everywhere.
Now Qutuz the Turk, who had been made king in Egypt,
when he heard that the King of Kings had gone far off,
and that Malik Nasir had been captured and sent to him,
and that Kitbuqa alone remained in Palestine with one myriad (ten thousand men),
gathered the armies of Egypt,
and went forth and met the Tatars in the meadow of Baysan, before Mount Tabor.
And the Tatars were broken,
and that Kitbuqa was killed in the battle,
and his sons were taken away as prisoners, on the 27th
of the ninth month of the Arabs, the year 658 {OCR?: 658}
of their reckoning.
And when this very news reached the King of Kings, he was enraged,
and resolved to uproot the entire kingdom of the Arabs from its roots.
And he commanded, and Malik Nasir was killed, together with his brother Malik Zahir and all who were with them,
on Wednesday... {OCR?}.
